mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes either wage inflation or policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in periods of UNRATE < 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals a manufacturing slowdown, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS growth) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND RSAFS monthly change > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months of coordinated PAYEMS and RSAFS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change < -0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE falls by more than 0.3pp for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12mo moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of HOUST below its 12-month moving average.
